questions.explanation: Moles: C = 40/12 = 3.33; H = 6.7/1 = 6.7; O = 53.3/16 = 3.33. Ratio = 1:2:1. Empirical formula = CH₂O (30). n = 180/30 = 6. Molecular formula = C₆H₁₂O₆.

questions.question: The process by which atoms are rearranged into different molecular structure in the petroleum refining process is referred to as
questions.explanation: Reforming rearranges the molecular structure of hydrocarbons (e.g., converting straight-chain to branched) to improve petrol quality.

questions.question: Which of the following is found in cotton
questions.explanation: Cotton fibers are made of pure cellulose, a natural polymer of glucose.

questions.question: The principal constituent of natural gas is
questions.explanation: Natural gas is primarily methane (CH₄), typically 70-90% by volume.

questions.question: When a solid substance disappears completely as a gas on heating, the substance is said to have undergone
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct transition from solid to gas without passing through the liquid state (e.g., iodine, ammonium chloride).

questions.question: A chemical reaction is always associated with
options: an increase in the composition of one of the substance
a change in the volume of the reactants
a change in the nature of the reactants
questions.explanation: A chemical reaction always involves the formation of new substances with different chemical properties from the reactants.

questions.question: If a solution contains 4.9g of tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid, calculate the amount of copper (II) oxide that will react with it [Cu = 64, O = 16, S = 32, H = 1]
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ + CuO → CuSO₄ + H₂O. Molar mass H₂SO₄ = 98; CuO = 80. Moles H₂SO₄ = 4.9/98 = 0.05 mol. Moles CuO = 0.05 mol. Mass = 0.05 × 80 = 4.0 g.

questions.question: What volume of gas is evolved at S.t.p if 2g of calcium trioxocarbonate (IV) is added to a solution of hydrochloric acid? [Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16, Molar volume = 22.4 dm³]
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. Molar mass CaCO₃ = 100. Moles = 2/100 = 0.02 mol. Volume CO₂ = 0.02 × 22.4 = 0.448 dm³ = 448 cm³.

questions.question: According to charles' law, the volume of a gas becomes zero at
questions.explanation: Charles's law: V ∝ T (absolute temperature). At absolute zero (-273°C or 0 K), the volume of an ideal gas theoretically becomes zero.

questions.question: It is difficult to achieve an orderly arrangement of the molecules of a gas because they?
options: have little force of attraction between them
can collide with one another in the container
questions.explanation: Gas molecules have negligible intermolecular forces, so they move randomly and freely, making orderly arrangement difficult.

questions.question: A given volume of methane diffuses in 20s. How long will it take the same volume of sulphur (IV) oxide to diffuse under the same conditions? [C = 12, H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Graham's law: t₁/t₂ = √(M₂/M₁). M(CH₄) = 16; M(SO₂) = 64. t(SO₂)/20 = √(64/16) = 2. t(SO₂) = 40 s.

questions.question: An electron can be added to a halogen atom to form a halide ion with
questions.explanation: Halogens have 7 valence electrons. Adding 1 electron gives a halide ion with a complete octet (8 valence electrons).

questions.question: The shape of s-orbitals is
questions.explanation: An s-orbital is spherically symmetric around the nucleus.

questions.question: ²²⁶₈₈Ra → ˣ₈₆Rn + α-particle. What is the value of x in the nuclear reaction above?
questions.explanation: Alpha decay: mass number decreases by 4, atomic number by 2. x = 226 − 4 = 222.

questions.question: The property of chlorine which causes hydrogen chloride to be more ionic than the chlorine molecules is its
questions.explanation: Chlorine's high electronegativity creates a polar (partially ionic) bond with hydrogen in HCl, unlike the non-polar Cl-Cl bond.

questions.question: Chlorine consisting of two isotopes of mass number 35 and 37 in the ratio 3:1 has an atomic mass of 35.5. Calculate the relative abundance of the isotopes of mass number 37
questions.explanation: Let abundance of ³⁷Cl = x, then ³⁵Cl = 3x. Total = 4x. (3x × 35 + x × 37)/(4x) = 35.5 → 142/4 = 35.5. ³⁷Cl abundance = x/4x × 100 = 25%.

questions.question: Which of the following mixture of gases is likely to burn in flame?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is flammable and burns in air. Neon is inert but doesn't prevent hydrogen from burning. The other options contain only non-flammable gases.

questions.question: Hardness of water is caused by the presence of ions of
questions.explanation: Water hardness is caused by dissolved calcium (Ca²⁺) and magnesium (Mg²⁺) ions.

questions.question: Pollution of underground water by metal ions is very likely in the soil that has high
questions.explanation: Acidic soil conditions increase the solubility of metal ions, allowing them to leach into groundwater.

questions.question: A carcinogenic substance is
questions.explanation: Asbestos dust is a known carcinogen, causing lung cancer and mesothelioma. Sawdust can also be carcinogenic but asbestos is more definitively linked to cancer.

questions.question: The solubility in moldm⁻³ of 20g of CuSO₄ dissolved in 100g of water at 18°C is [Cu = 64, S = 32, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass CuSO₄ = 160. Moles = 20/160 = 0.125 mol. Solubility = moles/volume of solvent = 0.125/0.1 = 1.25 mol/dm³.

questions.question: Calcium tetraoxosulphate (VI) dissolves in water only sparingly to form a
questions.explanation: Calcium sulphate is sparingly soluble. When it dissolves, the excess forms a precipitate — a solid that separates from solution.

questions.question: Which of the following compound is a normal salt?
questions.explanation: A normal salt is formed when all replaceable H atoms of an acid are replaced by a metal. Na₂CO₃ is a normal salt of carbonic acid (all H replaced). NaHS, NaHSO₄, and NaHCO₃ are acid salts.

questions.question: What volume of 0.5 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ will exactly neutralize 20cm³ of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaOH solution?
questions.explanation: 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Using C₁V₁/n₁ = C₂V₂/n₂: (0.5 × V)/1 = (0.1 × 20)/2. V = 2.0 cm³.

questions.question: The oxidation state of chlorine in HClO₄ is
ZnO(s) + CO(g) → Zn(s) + CO₂(g). In the reaction above, Zinc has been
questions.explanation: Zn goes from +2 in ZnO to 0 in Zn. This is a gain of electrons, so Zn is reduced.

questions.question: Which of the following acts as both reducing and oxidizing agent?
questions.explanation: SO₂ can act as both oxidizing and reducing agent because sulphur in SO₂ has an intermediate oxidation state (+4) and can be oxidized to +6 or reduced to 0/-2.

questions.question: In the electrolysis of brine, the anode is
questions.explanation: In the electrolysis of brine (concentrated NaCl), carbon (graphite) is used as the anode because it is inert and conducts electricity.

questions.question: The mass of silver deposited when a current of 10A is passed through a solution of silver salt for 4830s is [Ag = 108, 1F = 96500 Cmol⁻¹]
2CO(g) + O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g). Given that ΔH[CO] is -110.4 kJmol⁻¹ and ΔH[CO₂] is -393.0 kJmol⁻¹, the energy change for the reaction above is
Which of the following hydrogen halides has the highest entropy value?
questions.explanation: Entropy increases with molecular mass. HI (largest molecule) has the highest entropy value among the hydrogen halides.

questions.question: N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g). In the endothermic reaction above, more product formation will be favoured by
questions.explanation: The forward reaction produces more gas molecules (2 vs 1). By Le Chatelier's principle, decreasing pressure favours the side with more gas molecules — forward direction.

questions.question: Which of the following shows little or no net reaction when the volume of the system is decreased?
questions.explanation: If the number of gas moles is equal on both sides, changing pressure/volume has no effect on equilibrium. In option 1: 2 moles on both sides.

questions.question: The allotrope of carbon used in the decolourization of sugar is
questions.explanation: Charcoal (especially activated or animal charcoal) is used to decolourize sugar because of its high adsorption capacity due to its porous structure.

questions.question: Which of the following gases can be collected by the method of downward delivery?
questions.explanation: Downward delivery is used for gases that are denser than air (e.g., Cl₂). Upward delivery is for lighter gases (NH₃, H₂).

questions.question: When steam is passed over red-hot carbon, the substances produced are
questions.explanation: C + H₂O → CO + H₂ (water gas). This is an endothermic reaction producing carbon(II) oxide and hydrogen.

questions.question: Sulphur (IV) oxide bleaches by
questions.explanation: SO₂ bleaches by reduction — it removes oxygen from coloured substances, making them colourless. This bleaching is temporary (reversible).

questions.question: Carbon is tetravalent because
options: The electrons in both the 2s and 2p orbitals are equivalent
The electrons in all the orbitals of carbon are equivalent
All the atomic orbitals of carbon hybridize
questions.explanation: Carbon's 2s and 2p orbitals hybridize to form four equivalent sp³ hybrid orbitals, allowing carbon to form four bonds.

questions.question: Aluminium hydroxide is used in the dyeing industry as a
questions.explanation: Aluminium hydroxide acts as a mordant — it forms a complex with the dye that attaches to fabric, helping the dye fix and improving colourfastness.

questions.question: Alloys are best prepared by
options: Reducing and mixture of their metallic oxide
Cooling a molten mixture of the metals
questions.explanation: Alloys are best prepared by melting the metals together and cooling the molten mixture, allowing the metals to mix uniformly.

questions.question: Transition metals possess variable oxidation states because they have
options: A variable number of electrons in the p orbitals
questions.explanation: Transition metals have electrons in d orbitals that are close in energy to s electrons, allowing them to lose different numbers of electrons.

questions.question: Sodium metal is always kept under oil because it
options: Reacts vigorously on exposure to air
Reacts with oxygen and carbon (IV) oxide
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts vigorously on exposure to air (with oxygen and moisture), so it is stored under oil to prevent this reaction.

questions.question: Oxyacetylene flame is used for iron-welding because it
options: Makes the iron metals solidify very quickly
Combines with oxygen to give a pop sound
Evolves a lot of heat when burnt
Dissociates to produce carbon (IV) oxide and oxygen
questions.explanation: Oxyacetylene flame evolves a lot of heat (about 3000°C), high enough to melt and weld iron.

questions.question: The alkyl group can be represented by the general formula
questions.explanation: An alkyl group is derived from an alkane by removing one hydrogen. General formula: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁.

questions.question: An isomer of C₅H₁₂ is
questions.explanation: C₅H₁₂ has 3 isomers: n-pentane, 2-methylbutane, and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

questions.question: A characteristic of the alkane family is
questions.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons that undergo substitution reactions (e.g., chlorination) rather than addition.

questions.question: Which of these reagents can confirm the presence of a triple bond?
questions.explanation: Bromine water is decolourized by both alkenes and alkynes. However, to specifically confirm a triple bond, ammoniacal copper(I) chloride is used (forms red precipitate with terminal alkynes). But since only bromine water is listed as capable of reacting, the intended answer is option 1.

questions.question: Vulcanization involves the removal of
questions.explanation: Vulcanization involves the removal (or reaction) of double bonds in rubber by forming sulphur cross-links, making rubber harder and stronger.

questions.question: CH₃COOH(g) → CH₄(g) + CO₂(g). The reaction above is
questions.explanation: Decarboxylation is the removal of a carboxyl group (−COOH) as CO₂ from a molecule.

questions.question: C₂H₅OH(aq) → Y. If the above reaction takes place in conc. H₂SO₄ at 180°C, Y represents
questions.explanation: At 180°C with conc. H₂SO₄, ethanol undergoes dehydration to form ethene (C₂H₄). At 140°C, diethyl ether is formed.

questions.question: Alkanol + Alkanoic acid ⇌ Ester + Water. The reverse reaction above is known as
questions.explanation: The reverse of esterification is hydrolysis — the ester reacts with water to regenerate the alcohol and acid.

questions.question: In the production of soap, concentrated sodium chloride solution is added to
options: Decrease the solubility of the soap
questions.explanation: Adding concentrated NaCl (salting out) decreases the solubility of soap, causing it to precipitate out for easy separation.

questions.question: Which of the following equimolar solutions will have the highest pH?
questions.explanation: NaOH is a strong base, completely dissociating to give high [OH⁻] and the highest pH (about 14 for 1M solution).

questions.question: Which of the following ions require the largest quantity of electricity for discharge at an electrode?
questions.explanation: Charge needed = moles × electrons. Cl⁻: 4×1=4F; Na⁺: 3×1=3F; Cu²⁺: 2.5×2=5F; Al³⁺: 2×3=6F.

questions.question: Phenolphthalein in acidic solution is
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic solution (pH < 8.2) and pink in basic solution.

questions.question: When iron is exposed to moisture and it rusts, the value of ΔG for the reaction is
questions.explanation: Rusting is a spontaneous process, so ΔG is negative.

questions.question: In which of the following reactions can the oxidation number of the nitrogen be said to have increased?
questions.explanation: In NO, N = +2. In NO₂, N = +4. So oxidation number of N increases from +2 to +4.

questions.question: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O ΔH = -571kJ. In the equation above, how much heat will be liberated if 12.0g of hydrogen is burnt in excess oxygen?
questions.explanation: 4g of H₂ liberates 571 kJ. 12g of H₂ liberates (12/4) × 571 = 1713 kJ (negative sign indicates liberation).

questions.question: A concentrated solution containing H⁺, Cu²⁺, OH⁻ and Cl⁻ was electrolyzed using platinum electrodes. The ion that will be discharged at the cathode is?
questions.explanation: At the cathode, the ion with the highest discharge potential is discharged. Cu²⁺ is discharged in preference to H⁺ because copper is lower in the electrochemical series.

questions.question: When sulphur (IV) oxide is passed into a solution of sodium hydroxide for a long time, it eventually produces a solution of
questions.explanation: Excess SO₂ passed into NaOH gives NaHSO₃ (sodium hydrogen sulphite): SO₂ + NaOH → NaHSO₃.

questions.question: What is the correct IUPAC name for NO₂⁻?
questions.explanation: NO₂⁻ has N in oxidation state +3. IUPAC name: dioxonitrate(III) ion.

questions.question: What will happen if an aluminium spoon is used to stir a solution of iron (II) trioxonitrates (V)?
options: The spoon will be oxidized while the iron (II) ions will be reduced to the metal
The spoon will increase in size
The spoon will be reduced while the iron (II) ions will be oxidized
questions.explanation: Aluminium is more reactive than iron. Al is oxidized (goes into solution) while Fe²⁺ is reduced to Fe metal.

questions.question: The enzymes responsible for converting sucrose into two simple isomeric sugars is
questions.explanation: Invertase (sucrase) hydrolyzes sucrose into glucose and fructose (the two isomeric simple sugars).

questions.question: The decolourization of purple colour of tetraoxomanganate (VII) ion is a test for
questions.explanation: KMnO₄ (purple) is decolourized by alkenes (unsaturation). This is a test for unsaturation.

questions.question: Which of the following are structural isomers?
questions.explanation: Propanal (CH₃CH₂CHO) and propanone (CH₃COCH₃) both have the molecular formula C₃H₆O but different structures — they are isomers.

questions.question: In the purification of impure samples of ethyl ethanoate synthesized by esterification, concentrated sodium trioxocarbonate (IV) solution is used to remove
questions.explanation: Na₂CO₃ solution is basic and neutralizes acidic impurities (unreacted ethanoic acid and H₂SO₄ catalyst) from the ester.

questions.question: How many hydrogen atoms does a single ring cycloalkane have less than the corresponding open-chain alkane?
questions.explanation: Cycloalkanes have 2 fewer H atoms than the corresponding open-chain alkane because the ring closure removes 2 H atoms.

questions.question: Equal moles of ethyne and hydrogen iodide react to give
questions.explanation: HC≡CH + HI → CH₂=CHI. This is an addition reaction where HI adds across one of the triple bonds, forming a double bond.

questions.question: A substance that is used as a ripening agent for fruits is
questions.explanation: Ethene is a plant hormone that naturally triggers fruit ripening and is used commercially as a ripening agent.

questions.question: When water boilers are used for long period of time, the solid substances left behind as scale are
questions.explanation: Boiler scale consists of magnesium silicate and rust (iron oxide) from the reaction of hard water minerals with the boiler metal at high temperatures.

questions.question: 25cm³ of a mixture of noble gases was obtained from air after the removal of other constituents. What was the original volume of air?
questions.explanation: Noble gases constitute about 1% of air. If 25 cm³ is 1%, original volume = 25 × 100 = 2,500 cm³.

questions.question: The solubility curve shows the variation of solute concentration with
questions.explanation: A solubility curve shows how the solubility of a solute varies with temperature.

questions.question: The air around smelting industries is likely to contain
questions.explanation: Smelting industries release SO₂, CO₂ and other gases. The correct option should contain SO₂ and CO₂ as major pollutants.

questions.question: Kerosene is commonly used to remove the red colour stain of palm oil from cloths because it
options: helps to spread the oil over a larger surface area
react with the oil to form an odourless compound
makes the oil evaporate easily by dissolving it
helps to dilute the oil and reduce its colour
questions.explanation: Kerosene is a non-polar solvent that dissolves the oil, allowing it to be washed away from the fabric.

questions.question: The gas that is the most dangerous pollutant to human is
questions.explanation: Hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) is extremely toxic, affecting the respiratory and nervous systems even at low concentrations.

questions.question: Natural water collected from rivers and ponds contain oxygen, carbon (IV) oxide and
questions.explanation: Natural water contains dissolved atmospheric gases: oxygen, carbon dioxide, and nitrogen.

questions.question: How many moles of limestone will be required to produce 5.6g of CaO? [Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Molar mass CaO = 56. Moles CaO = 5.6/56 = 0.10 mol. From equation, 1 mol CaCO₃ gives 1 mol CaO. So moles limestone = 0.10 mol.

questions.question: The shape of the hydrocarbon compound CH₄ is
questions.explanation: CH₄ has sp³ hybridization, giving a tetrahedral shape with bond angles of 109.5°.

questions.question: Which of these properties gives a solid its definite shape?
questions.explanation: Strong intermolecular attraction holds particles in fixed positions, giving solids a definite shape.

questions.question: Sugar is separated from its impurities by
questions.explanation: Crystallization is used to purify sugar — sugar crystallizes out while impurities remain in solution.

questions.question: The component of an atom that contributes least to its mass is the
questions.explanation: The electron has a mass about 1/1840 of a proton, so it contributes negligibly to atomic mass.

questions.question: An element will readily form an electrovalent compound if its electron configuration is
questions.explanation: Configuration 2, 8, 1 indicates an alkali metal (like Na) with one valence electron, which it readily loses to form an electrovalent (ionic) compound.

questions.question: A heterogenous mixture can be defined as any mixture
options: of a solute and a solvent
questions.explanation: A heterogeneous mixture has non-uniform composition — different parts have different properties.

questions.question: The pressure of 100cm³ of oxygen at 35°C is 750mmHg. What will be the volume of gas if the pressure is reduced to 100mmHg without changing the temperature?
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂. 750 × 100 = 100 × V₂. V₂ = 750 cm³.

questions.question: I. Treatment of cancer II. Detection of leakages in water mains III. Detection of the ages of ancient tools IV. Preparation of drugs. Which combination of the above refers to the uses of radioactive isotopes?
questions.explanation: Radioactive isotopes are used in: cancer treatment (I), leak detection (II), radiocarbon dating (III), and drug preparation (IV). So I, II, III and IV.

questions.question: What is the valence shell electron configuration of the element with atomic number 17?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 17 = Chlorine. Full config: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁵. Valence shell (n=3) config: 3s² 3p⁵.

questions.question: The density of a certain gas is 1.98gdm⁻³ at s.t.p. What is the molecular mass of the gas?
questions.explanation: Molar volume at s.t.p = 22.4 dm³. Molecular mass = density × molar volume = 1.98 × 22.4 = 44.0 g.

questions.question: When pure aluminium metal is heated to red hot in the presence of nitrogen gas, the compound formed is
questions.explanation: 2Al + N₂ → 2AlN (aluminium nitride).

questions.question: A dense white fume is formed when ammonia gas reacts with
questions.explanation: NH₃(g) + HCl(g) → NH₄Cl(s). The solid ammonium chloride appears as dense white fumes.

questions.question: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) ΔH = -90 kJ. In the equation above, the yield of ammonia can be decreased by
options: removing the ammonia as it is formed
questions.explanation: The reaction is exothermic (ΔH = -90 kJ). By Le Chatelier's principle, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium backward, decreasing NH₃ yield.

questions.question: The gas that can be dried using concentrated tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid is
questions.explanation: Conc. H₂SO₄ can dry SO₂ (it doesn't react with it). It cannot dry HBr (oxidizes it), H₂S (oxidizes it), or NH₃ (reacts to form (NH₄)₂SO₄).

questions.question: NH₄Cl(s) ⇌ NH₃(g) + HCl(g). The reaction above can only attain equilibrium if
options: one of the products is removed
it is in a closed system
questions.explanation: Equilibrium can only be attained in a closed system where products cannot escape.

questions.question: The most suitable metal that can be used as lightning conductor is?
questions.explanation: Copper is the most suitable metal for lightning conductors — it has excellent electrical conductivity, is corrosion-resistant, and is cost-effective compared to silver.

questions.question: In the diagram above which of the curves illustrates Arrhenius' law?
questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation plot (ln k vs 1/T) gives a straight line with negative slope. Curve X represents this relationship.

questions.question: The most abundant element on the earth's crust is
questions.explanation: Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust, making up about 46.6% by mass.

questions.question: Metalloids are also referred to as
questions.explanation: Metalloids (e.g., silicon, germanium) are also called semi-metals because they have properties intermediate between metals and non-metals.

questions.question: The ores that can be concentrated by flotation are
questions.explanation: Flotation is used to concentrate sulphide ores (e.g., galena PbS, zinc blende ZnS) because sulphide minerals are preferentially wetted by oil.

questions.question: The property used in the industrial preparation of nitrogen and oxygen from air is?
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation of liquid air separates N₂ and O₂ based on their different boiling points (N₂: -196°C; O₂: -183°C).

questions.question: In a flame test for calcium, the flame appears
options: green when viewed through a blue glass
blue when viewed through a blue glass
orange-red when viewed through a blue glass
brick-red when viewed through a blue-glass
questions.explanation: Calcium gives a brick-red flame. When viewed through blue glass, it appears green (blue glass filters out other colours).

questions.question: Which of the following alloys contain iron?
questions.explanation: Steel (Fe + C) and permalloy (Fe + Ni) both contain iron. Duralumin (Al alloy), brass (Cu-Zn), bronze (Cu-Sn), and soft solder (Sn-Pb) do not.

questions.question: To obtain pure carbon (II) oxide from its mixture with carbon (IV) oxide, the mixture should be
questions.explanation: CO₂ is acidic and reacts with NaOH to form Na₂CO₃, while CO is neutral and passes through. Bubbling through NaOH solution removes CO₂, leaving pure CO.

questions.question: The raw materials used for the smelting of iron ore in a furnace is
questions.explanation: Limestone (CaCO₃) is used in the blast furnace to remove silica impurities as slag (calcium silicate).

questions.question: On heating, which of the following compounds will decompose to the free metal, nitrogen (IV) oxide and oxygen?
questions.explanation: AgNO₃ decomposes to silver metal, NO₂, and O₂: 2AgNO₃ → 2Ag + 2NO₂ + O₂. Ca and Cu nitrates give oxides, not free metals.

questions.question: The group IA metals are not found free in nature because they
options: have high melting and boiling point
questions.explanation: Group IA (alkali) metals are very reactive — they readily lose their single valence electron and react with water, oxygen, etc., so they are never found free in nature.

questions.question: Carbon exist naturally in the combined state as?
questions.explanation: Wood is a combined form of carbon (cellulose, lignin). Graphite, coal, and diamond are free forms (allotropes) of carbon.

questions.question: The efficiency of a solid catalyst to increase reaction rates depends on its
questions.explanation: A solid catalyst works at its surface. The greater the surface area, the more active sites available, and the more efficient the catalyst.

questions.question: Dynamic equilibrium describes a situation where
options: a reaction gives back the reactant
the concentration of the reactant and products is equal
both forward and reverse reactions proceed at the same rate
questions.explanation: In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions occur at the same rate, so concentrations remain constant.

questions.question: The ion that will give a white precipitate with aqueous NaOH and soluble in excess of the base is
questions.explanation: Zn²⁺ gives a white precipitate of Zn(OH)₂ with NaOH, which dissolves in excess NaOH to form zincate ion [Zn(OH)₄]²⁻.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of substance will react further with oxygen to form a higher oxide?
questions.explanation: SO₂ can be further oxidized to SO₃, and NO can be oxidized to NO₂. So SO₂ and NO both form higher oxides.

questions.question: The characteristic colour of the flame shown when a copper salt moistened with concentrated hydrochloric acid on a platinum wire is put on bunsen burner is
questions.explanation: Copper salts give a green (blue-green) flame in a flame test.

questions.question: In the industrial production of H₂ from natural gas the CO₂ produced along with the H₂ is removed by
options: passing the mixture into lime water
questions.explanation: CO₂ is removed from the gas mixture by washing under pressure with water or other solvents in which CO₂ is highly soluble.

questions.question: The sulphide which is insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid is
questions.explanation: CuS (copper(II) sulphide) has a very low Ksp and is insoluble in dilute HCl. FeS, ZnS, and Na₂S are soluble.

questions.question: Which of the following typically represents a photochemical reaction?
options: Formation of water from hydrogen and oxygen molecules
Conversion of dinitrogen (IV) oxide to nitrogen (IV) oxide
Decomposition of calcium hydroxide to its oxide
Conversion of silver halides to grey metallic silver
questions.explanation: Conversion of silver halides to silver metal is a photochemical reaction — it requires light energy (used in photography).

questions.question: The gas obtained as a product of anaerobic action on organic matter buried in the earth is?
questions.explanation: Anaerobic decomposition of organic matter produces methane (CH₄) as the main product (biogas).

questions.question: Nigerian crude oil is described as light crude because of its
questions.explanation: Nigerian crude oil is light and sweet because of its low sulphur content and low density.

questions.question: An example of aliphatic unsaturated hydrocarbon is
questions.explanation: Propene (CH₂=CHCH₃) is an aliphatic unsaturated hydrocarbon (alkene). Benzene is aromatic; pentane is saturated; butanol is an alcohol.

questions.question: Which of the following has an isomer?
questions.explanation: C₄H₁₀ (butane) has two isomers: n-butane and 2-methylpropane (isobutane). The others (C₂H₆, C₂H₄, C₆H₆) do not have structural isomers.

questions.question: CH₃-CH₂-C≡CH. The hybridization in the compound above is
questions.explanation: CH₃ and CH₂ carbons are sp³ hybridized. The C≡C carbons are sp hybridized. So the compound contains both sp³ and sp.

questions.question: One mole of a hydrocarbon contains 36g of carbon and its vapour density is 20. The structure of the hydrocarbon is
questions.explanation: Molecular mass = 2 × V.D. = 40. Mass of C = 36g → moles C = 3. Mass of H = 40 - 36 = 4g → moles H = 4. Formula = C₃H₄. This is CH₃C≡CH (propyne).

questions.question: An emulsion may be produced by shaking a detergent solution with
questions.explanation: Palm oil is a non-polar oil. Detergent (emulsifying agent) helps disperse it in water to form an emulsion.

questions.question: The products of the combustion of candle wax are?
questions.explanation: Candle wax is a hydrocarbon. Complete combustion produces CO₂ and H₂O.

questions.question: When 50cm³ of a saturated solution of sugar of molar mass 342 g at 40°C was evaporated to dryness, 34.2g of dry solid was obtained. The solubility of sugar at 40°C is
questions.explanation: Moles = 34.2/342 = 0.1 mol. Volume = 50 cm³ = 0.05 dm³. Solubility = 0.1/0.05 = 2.0 mol/dm³.

questions.question: Which of the following results in the fall of acid rain?
questions.explanation: Acid rain is caused primarily by oxides of sulphur (SO₂ and SO₃) and nitrogen oxides dissolving in rainwater to form acids.

questions.question: Water has the ability to dissolve almost all substance because its molecules has a structure with
options: one positive end and one neutral end
one positive end and one negative end
questions.explanation: Water is a polar molecule with one positive end (H) and one negative end (O), allowing it to dissolve both ionic and polar substances.

questions.question: When a crystal was added to the clear solution of its salt, the crystal did not dissolve and the solution remained unchanged. This showed that the solution was
questions.explanation: In a saturated solution, no more solute can dissolve. Adding a crystal results in no change — the crystal remains undissolved.

questions.question: A particle that contains 11 protons, 12 neutrons and 10 electrons is probably a
questions.explanation: 11 protons = Na (sodium, a metal). 10 electrons means it has lost 1 electron, so it's a positive ion (Na⁺). It's a metallic ion.

questions.question: A difference between chemical and physical change is that in a chemical change
questions.explanation: A chemical change always results in the formation of new substances with different properties.

questions.question: The volume of 2.5 moles of oxygen at s.t.p is [Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p = 22.4 dm³]
questions.explanation: Volume = moles × molar volume = 2.5 × 22.4 = 56.0 dm³.

questions.question: Nuclear fission involves the splitting of a heavy element into two nuclei of
options: nearly equal masses with a release of energy and radiation
equal masses with a release of energy
equal masses with a release of energy and radiation
unequal masses without any release of energy
questions.explanation: Nuclear fission splits a heavy nucleus into two nuclei of nearly equal masses, releasing energy and radiation.

questions.question: What is the molar mass of a substance, if 0.4 mole of the substance has a mass of 25.0g?
questions.explanation: Molar mass = mass/moles = 25.0/0.4 = 62.5 g.

questions.question: The element with the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p³ is
questions.explanation: 1s² 2s² 2p³ has 7 electrons = nitrogen (N).

questions.question: A decrease in atomic size and an increase in nuclear charge across a period lead to
options: an increase in the tendency to lose electron
a decrease in covalency in bond formation
questions.explanation: Across a period, atoms become smaller and nuclear charge increases, making them less willing to lose electrons. This is a decrease in electropositivity.

questions.question: The order in which a mixture of sand, ammonium chloride and sodium chloride can be separated is
questions.explanation: Correct order: Sublimation (removes NH₄Cl) → Dissolution (add water, NaCl dissolves) → Filtration (removes sand) → Evaporation (recovers NaCl).

questions.question: The idea of planetary electron was that of
questions.explanation: Rutherford proposed the planetary model where electrons orbit the nucleus like planets around the sun (1911).
